sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Each pair addresses a different part of the model: attention, information, decision criteria and your approach to the outside world.

E/I concerns whether attention and energy tend toward the outer world or inner reflection. S/N concerns concrete experience or patterns and possibilities. T/F concerns logical consistency or values and the people affected. J/P concerns settling an outward arrangement or keeping options open.

In a fictional example, a colleague asks three teams what they need before planning a shared session. The assignment may require consultation regardless of the colleague’s preferences.

In type dynamics, an extraverted type’s dominant process faces outward. ENFJ’s J indicates a judging process and its F identifies Feeling, so the dominant is extraverted Feeling (Fe). Introverted Intuition (Ni) is auxiliary. These roles do not measure warmth or leadership.

### How to read the four ENFJ preferences

Use the questions to reflect on situations where you had room to choose. Pay attention to what mattered as well as what you did.

| Preference | What is more likely to be the basis when there is a choice |
| --- | --- |
| E · Extraversion | With time to reflect, does talking the issue through or thinking it over privately draw your attention more naturally? |
| N · Intuition | Do the connections and possibilities or the details and past examples draw your attention? |
| F · Feeling | How much weight do you give to the effects on people and to a criterion that applies across cases? |
| J · Judging | Which commitments would you prefer to settle, and which would you leave open for new information? |

Both answers can be useful in the same decision. Deadlines and responsibilities can also affect the choices available.

### The four function positions for ENFJ

This page lists Fe as dominant, Ni as auxiliary, Se as tertiary and Ti as inferior. The positions describe the model and cannot tell you what someone will do first.

In the model, Fe weighs values and effects on people in the external situation. Ni looks for an underlying pattern. Se attends to what is observable now. Ti checks internal consistency. A decision can involve several of these considerations.

The Foundation lists ENFJ’s tertiary Sensing as Se or Si. This page uses Se. The dominant and auxiliary descriptions stay the same across the two notations.

### Where the A/T suffix sits for ENFJ

Assertive (-A) and Turbulent (-T) are the ends of 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity scale. They describe self-assurance and responses to pressure. The official MBTI uses four letters. See [ENFJ-A](/en/personality/enfj-a), [ENFJ-T](/en/personality/enfj-t) and the [same-type comparison](/en/personality/enfj-a-vs-enfj-t).
sections.title: ENFJ letters and framework

sections.body_md:
Summarise what a group agreed on and ask each person to confirm what they are willing to do.

In a fictional book group, twenty people suggest directions for next quarter. Group the suggestions, note which priorities still differ and ask who is willing to lead a session. A vote on the books does not assign a session leader.

Instead of signing a colleague up to present, ask whether they want to. Make clear that they can decline.

| Observation | Possible choice and cost | One concrete move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Summarising a discussion | A short summary can hide a view held by only a few people. | Show which comments support the summary and which differ. |
| Gathering views | You may miss someone who had less opportunity to speak. | Ask what they want to add without assuming their answer. |
| Weighing priorities | Protecting one priority can cost someone time. | Say who would do the extra work. |
| Inviting participation | Enthusiasm can sound like a promise. | Confirm who is willing to do the next task. |
| Handling disagreement | A polite summary can obscure the actual point of disagreement. | State that point in a sentence people can respond to. |
| Handover | A task can stay with its original owner longer than planned. | Agree when the next person takes over. |
sections.title: ENFJ core patterns, value and counterexamples

sections.body_md:
Try a coordination task and check whether you would want to repeat it. Ask how much authority the role gives you, who provides feedback and who is responsible for the result.

In a fictional onboarding week, write the first-day briefing, draft a way for a new colleague to ask questions and plan how to gather feedback on Friday. Note which parts you would want to do regularly.

| Direction to explore | Try-out and job entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Training and mentoring | Write a short onboarding guide. Ask a willing reader to mark what is unclear. [Training and development specialists](/en/career/jobs/training-and-development-specialists#fit) |
| External communication | Explain a fictional product change in terms of what the customer needs to do. [Public relations specialists](/en/career/jobs/public-relations-specialists#fit) |
| Events and projects | Draft a timetable for a forty-person event and mark who needs to be present at each stage. [Meeting, convention and event planners](/en/career/jobs/meeting-convention-and-event-planners#fit) |
| People and hiring | Using a fictional vacancy, draft the same job-related interview questions for each candidate. [Human resources specialists](/en/career/jobs/human-resources-specialists#fit) |
| Community and charity | Read a fictional donor follow-up and summarise what the donor asked and what still needs an answer. [Fundraisers](/en/career/jobs/fundraisers#fit) |

Ask who makes decisions, how often the team gets feedback and who handles unexpected requests. Check the answers against an example of the team’s work.

Working with people is one part of coordination. Check how often plans change, how approvals work and how much uninterrupted time the job allows.

### What an ENFJ try-out should record

Record what you did, how long it took, which decisions you owned, what feedback you received and what you would want to repeat.

Account for differences in group size, time or authority before comparing two trials.

Note where coordination got stuck and what changed the plan. Use this to understand the work and what support it requires.
sections.title: ENFJ work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
Communication in a relationship can start with one move: replace "I've arranged it for you" with "how would you like to arrange it, and which part can I take?"

In a fictional family planning discussion, ask whether travelling between several homes would be tiring before suggesting a closer meeting place.

If a friend says they have had enough of the week, ask whether they want to talk or would like help with something.

Before contacting someone on another person’s behalf, ask whether they want you to do it. They may prefer to handle it themselves.

### ENFJ: turning coordination into a question

Make it clear which part is a proposal and where the other person can say no.

Describe what you noticed, propose a change and ask who decides. For example: “Three teams asked to change this form. I can draft a new version. Who needs to approve it?”

If someone says either option is fine, clarify whether they are delegating the decision or offering to do the work. Record the work as pending until the person who will do it confirms.
sections.title: ENFJ relationships and communication

sections.body_md:
Type cannot predict how tense someone will feel or how quickly they will recover. If you are taking on more than you can manage, check which commitments you actually own.

Separate work you agreed to do, requests you have not accepted and decisions that require someone else’s approval.

In a fictional example, you have two free evenings and two requests for help. Decide what you can realistically offer and tell each person when you can do it.

If poor sleep or distress persists or affects everyday life, consider speaking with a qualified professional.
sections.title: ENFJ stress and recovery

sections.body_md:
Compare what you assumed people wanted with what they actually said.

Write down three decisions from the week. For each, record your assumption, what it rested on and how the other person responded.

Include cases where someone declined an offer, took on a task or asked you to reconsider. Compare who had authority, how much time was available and what the task required.

For a low-risk exercise, draft an event responsibility list and ask people to confirm their own tasks. Mark unconfirmed tasks as open. Review what changed and whether anyone still needs to be asked.
sections.title: ENFJ observation practice

sections.body_md:
Compare the neighbouring types in the same task, with the same information and the same deadline.

ENFJ differs from INFJ only on E/I, from ESFJ only on S/N and from ENFP only on J/P. Either type in a pair can take the same action.

### ENFJ against its neighbours on the preference axes

| Neighbouring type | Shared and different | Axis | What each may lean on in the same situation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj) | Share N, F and J. | E/I | Does attention tend toward the outer situation or inner reflection? Either type can discuss the issue or think it over privately. |
| [ESFJ profile](/en/personality/esfj) | Share E, F and J. | S/N | Does the person give more weight to concrete observations and experience, or to patterns and possibilities? |
| [ENFP profile](/en/personality/enfp) | Share E, N and F. | J/P | With the same information, which arrangements would each person settle or leave open? |

The three links below describe 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity aspect. Assertive and Turbulent concern self-assurance and responses to pressure. They fall outside the four official MBTI letters.

- [ENFJ-A: self-assurance and response to pressure](/en/personality/enfj-a)
- [ENFJ-T: self-doubt and sensitivity to stress](/en/personality/enfj-t)
- [ENFJ-A and ENFJ-T: the suffix and its limits](/en/personality/enfj-a-vs-enfj-t)
- [INFJ profile: comparing the E/I direction of attention](/en/personality/infj)
- [ESFJ profile: comparing the N/S information preference](/en/personality/esfj)
- [ENFP profile: comparing J/P in the outer arrangement](/en/personality/enfp)
- [Browse the 16 types: compare other base descriptions](/en/personality)

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The four preferences follow the Myers–Briggs framework. See the [Foundation’s type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) for the functions. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Fe–Ni–Se–Ti. The Foundation also allows Si for tertiary Sensing. The positions describe the model and cannot predict the order of actions or how well someone can do a task.

**Editorial fiction.** The cross-team discussion, book group, onboarding week, conversations and coordination exercises are fictional examples. They illustrate choices without measuring anyone’s behaviour.

**Scope.** Use these descriptions for reflection. They cannot establish ability, career fit or relationship outcomes. [Erford et al. (2025), Table 5](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) lists 75 ENFJs among 3,009 people (2.5%) in the U.S. Form M manual sample. The authors excluded studies presented in the manuals from their analyses and used the manual sample as a separate comparison. It cannot estimate today’s worldwide prevalence.

E/I concerns whether attention and energy tend toward the outer world or inner reflection. S/N concerns concrete experience or patterns and possibilities. T/F concerns logical consistency or values and the people affected. J/P concerns settling an outward arrangement or keeping options open.

In a fictional example, a colleague asks three teams what they need before planning a shared session. The assignment may require consultation regardless of the colleague’s preferences.

In type dynamics, an extraverted type’s dominant process faces outward. ENFJ’s J indicates a judging process and its F identifies Feeling, so the dominant is extraverted Feeling (Fe). Introverted Intuition (Ni) is auxiliary. These roles do not measure warmth or leadership.

### How to read the four ENFJ preferences

Use the questions to reflect on situations where you had room to choose. Pay attention to what mattered as well as what you did.

| Preference | What is more likely to be the basis when there is a choice |
| --- | --- |
| E · Extraversion | With time to reflect, does talking the issue through or thinking it over privately draw your attention more naturally? |
| N · Intuition | Do the connections and possibilities or the details and past examples draw your attention? |
| F · Feeling | How much weight do you give to the effects on people and to a criterion that applies across cases? |
| J · Judging | Which commitments would you prefer to settle, and which would you leave open for new information? |

Both answers can be useful in the same decision. Deadlines and responsibilities can also affect the choices available.

### The four function positions for ENFJ

This page lists Fe as dominant, Ni as auxiliary, Se as tertiary and Ti as inferior. The positions describe the model and cannot tell you what someone will do first.

In the model, Fe weighs values and effects on people in the external situation. Ni looks for an underlying pattern. Se attends to what is observable now. Ti checks internal consistency. A decision can involve several of these considerations.

The Foundation lists ENFJ’s tertiary Sensing as Se or Si. This page uses Se. The dominant and auxiliary descriptions stay the same across the two notations.

### Where the A/T suffix sits for ENFJ

Assertive (-A) and Turbulent (-T) are the ends of 16Personalities’ NERIS Identity scale. They describe self-assurance and responses to pressure. The official MBTI uses four letters. See [ENFJ-A](/en/personality/enfj-a), [ENFJ-T](/en/personality/enfj-t) and the [same-type comparison](/en/personality/enfj-a-vs-enfj-t).

sections.body_md:
Summarise what a group agreed on and ask each person to confirm what they are willing to do.

In a fictional book group, twenty people suggest directions for next quarter. Group the suggestions, note which priorities still differ and ask who is willing to lead a session. A vote on the books does not assign a session leader.

Instead of signing a colleague up to present, ask whether they want to. Make clear that they can decline.

| Observation | Possible choice and cost | One concrete move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Summarising a discussion | A short summary can hide a view held by only a few people. | Show which comments support the summary and which differ. |
| Gathering views | You may miss someone who had less opportunity to speak. | Ask what they want to add without assuming their answer. |
| Weighing priorities | Protecting one priority can cost someone time. | Say who would do the extra work. |
| Inviting participation | Enthusiasm can sound like a promise. | Confirm who is willing to do the next task. |
| Handling disagreement | A polite summary can obscure the actual point of disagreement. | State that point in a sentence people can respond to. |
| Handover | A task can stay with its original owner longer than planned. | Agree when the next person takes over. |

sections.body_md:
Try a coordination task and check whether you would want to repeat it. Ask how much authority the role gives you, who provides feedback and who is responsible for the result.

In a fictional onboarding week, write the first-day briefing, draft a way for a new colleague to ask questions and plan how to gather feedback on Friday. Note which parts you would want to do regularly.

| Direction to explore | Try-out and job entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Training and mentoring | Write a short onboarding guide. Ask a willing reader to mark what is unclear. [Training and development specialists](/en/career/jobs/training-and-development-specialists#fit) |
| External communication | Explain a fictional product change in terms of what the customer needs to do. [Public relations specialists](/en/career/jobs/public-relations-specialists#fit) |
| Events and projects | Draft a timetable for a forty-person event and mark who needs to be present at each stage. [Meeting, convention and event planners](/en/career/jobs/meeting-convention-and-event-planners#fit) |
| People and hiring | Using a fictional vacancy, draft the same job-related interview questions for each candidate. [Human resources specialists](/en/career/jobs/human-resources-specialists#fit) |
| Community and charity | Read a fictional donor follow-up and summarise what the donor asked and what still needs an answer. [Fundraisers](/en/career/jobs/fundraisers#fit) |

Ask who makes decisions, how often the team gets feedback and who handles unexpected requests. Check the answers against an example of the team’s work.

Working with people is one part of coordination. Check how often plans change, how approvals work and how much uninterrupted time the job allows.

### What an ENFJ try-out should record

Record what you did, how long it took, which decisions you owned, what feedback you received and what you would want to repeat.

Account for differences in group size, time or authority before comparing two trials.

Note where coordination got stuck and what changed the plan. Use this to understand the work and what support it requires.
sections.title: ENFJ work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
Communication in a relationship can start with one move: replace "I've arranged it for you" with "how would you like to arrange it, and which part can I take?"

In a fictional family planning discussion, ask whether travelling between several homes would be tiring before suggesting a closer meeting place.

If a friend says they have had enough of the week, ask whether they want to talk or would like help with something.

Before contacting someone on another person’s behalf, ask whether they want you to do it. They may prefer to handle it themselves.

### ENFJ: turning coordination into a question

Make it clear which part is a proposal and where the other person can say no.

Describe what you noticed, propose a change and ask who decides. For example: “Three teams asked to change this form. I can draft a new version. Who needs to approve it?”

If someone says either option is fine, clarify whether they are delegating the decision or offering to do the work. Record the work as pending until the person who will do it confirms.

Type cannot predict how tense someone will feel or how quickly they will recover. If you are taking on more than you can manage, check which commitments you actually own.

Separate work you agreed to do, requests you have not accepted and decisions that require someone else’s approval.

In a fictional example, you have two free evenings and two requests for help. Decide what you can realistically offer and tell each person when you can do it.

If poor sleep or distress persists or affects everyday life, consider speaking with a qualified professional.

sections.body_md:
Compare what you assumed people wanted with what they actually said.

Write down three decisions from the week. For each, record your assumption, what it rested on and how the other person responded.

Include cases where someone declined an offer, took on a task or asked you to reconsider. Compare who had authority, how much time was available and what the task required.

For a low-risk exercise, draft an event responsibility list and ask people to confirm their own tasks. Mark unconfirmed tasks as open. Review what changed and whether anyone still needs to be asked.

The manual column in Table 5 of [Erford et al. (2025)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) lists 75 ENFJs in the US MBTI Form M manual sample of 3,009 people, which is 2.5%.

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The four preferences follow the Myers–Briggs framework. See the [Foundation’s type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) for the functions. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Fe–Ni–Se–Ti. The Foundation also allows Si for tertiary Sensing. The positions describe the model and cannot predict the order of actions or how well someone can do a task.

**Editorial fiction.** The cross-team discussion, book group, onboarding week, conversations and coordination exercises are fictional examples. They illustrate choices without measuring anyone’s behaviour.

**Scope.** Use these descriptions for reflection. They cannot establish ability, career fit or relationship outcomes. [Erford et al. (2025), Table 5](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) lists 75 ENFJs among 3,009 people (2.5%) in the U.S. Form M manual sample. The authors excluded studies presented in the manuals from their analyses and used the manual sample as a separate comparison. It cannot estimate today’s worldwide prevalence.

The manual column in Table 5 of [Erford et al. (2025)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) lists 75 ENFJs in the US MBTI Form M manual sample of 3,009 people, which is 2.5%.

The 2.5% figure is specific to the U.S. manual sample. Table 5 reports a separate study aggregate in another column. Neither gives current worldwide prevalence or counts for NERIS A and T.
items.question: Is ENFJ rare, and what share of the US MBTI Form M sample is it?

items.answer:
Ask whether the person is willing, has time and has accepted that specific task. A positive reaction can leave any of those questions open.

Ask, “Can you take page two by Wednesday, or do you need to check first?” If they need to check, leave the task marked as pending.
items.question: How can ENFJ tell whether someone has really agreed?

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The four preferences follow the Myers–Briggs framework. See the [Foundation’s type dynamics table](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) for the functions. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Fe–Ni–Se–Ti. The Foundation also allows Si for tertiary Sensing. The positions describe the model and cannot predict the order of actions or how well someone can do a task.

**Editorial fiction.** The cross-team discussion, book group, onboarding week, conversations and coordination exercises are fictional examples. They illustrate choices without measuring anyone’s behaviour.

**Scope.** Use these descriptions for reflection. They cannot establish ability, career fit or relationship outcomes. [Erford et al. (2025), Table 5](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) lists 75 ENFJs among 3,009 people (2.5%) in the U.S. Form M manual sample. The authors excluded studies presented in the manuals from their analyses and used the manual sample as a separate comparison. It cannot estimate today’s worldwide prevalence.
